name: less
one_line: view a file or output one screen at a time
plain: `less` shows a long file or long command output one page at a time. You can scroll up and down, search, and quit. It is also the pager that `man` uses, so every key you learn here works inside man pages.
Unlike an editor it never changes the file, and it opens big files instantly because it does not read everything first.
when: Read a big log or text file.
Page through the output of any command (command | less).
Search a file for a word and jump between matches.
Follow a growing log like tail -f (press F).

examples.title: Open a file
examples.explain: Use Space or f for next page, b for previous, q to quit.

examples.title: Page any command's output
examples.explain: Pipe the output into less when it is longer than the screen.

examples.title: Search while reading
examples.cmd: /error   then n for next, N for previous, ?error to search backwards
examples.explain: Type / then the text and Enter. Matches are highlighted.

examples.title: Show line numbers
examples.explain: -N prefixes each line with its number: handy when you need to say 'line 42'.

examples.title: Do not wrap long lines
examples.explain: -S chops long lines instead of wrapping; scroll sideways with the arrow keys.

examples.title: Keep colours from a command
examples.explain: -R passes colour codes through instead of showing ESC characters.

examples.title: Follow a log live
examples.explain: +F starts in follow mode like tail -f. Press Ctrl+C to stop following and scroll, then F to follow again.

examples.title: Start at a pattern
examples.explain: -p opens the file at the first match.

examples.title: Jump around
examples.explain: Number then g goes to that line; a percentage goes to that part of the file.

examples.title: Show only lines with a word
examples.explain: Inside less, & filters the display to lines matching the pattern. &  with nothing resets it.

mistakes: Typing q when you wanted to type / : q always quits.
Expecting less to edit: it only reads (press v to open an editor).
Piping into less and then wondering why the command already finished: the pipe waits for you to quit.
Not knowing F follows a log: it is the live tail you often need.
try: Open /etc/passwd with less -N and search for root.
Page a long man page and use / and n.
Use less +F on a log that is being written (try ping localhost > /tmp/p.log).
